0.label: head_finial_with_marks
0.description: A carved head on a collared shaft: a cross-hatched cap, lidded eyes, broad nose, full lips, small bosses on the cheeks and marks at the temples, a twisted collar at the neck.
0.iconography: A head (orí) — the seat of destiny in Yoruba thought — with facial marks (ilà) that name a lineage or town, and a beaded cap of rank. As a finial it tops a staff or post.

panel.title: Modakeke head finial with cap and facial marks
panel.object_type: staff or post finial (object in the round)
panel.summary: A single carved head on a collared shaft, photographed on its own: cross-hatched cap, strong facial features, cheek bosses and a twisted collar.

register_readings.reading: Cap, face, collar and the start of the shaft, top to bottom.

panel.composition: Frontal and symmetrical; ornament at the top (cap) and bottom (collar) frames a plain, modelled face.
panel.narrative: A person of consequence reduced to the head, the part that carries destiny. Its facial marks are the one element that could tie it to a named lineage, if compared with documented Ife and Oyo marks. The twisted collar repeats the rope border used on door and tray rims.
panel.hypotheses: Neutral. Facial marks are a local sign system worth recording but are not a count.
cross_panel_links: Rope-twist collar: the plait and guilloche borders of FoA_04-5578 and FoA_04-5587.
uncertainties: The cheek bosses could be damage on the print.
